explain.discountOnly: This unit has been in {store} for {age} days. A {pct} discount lifts the 60-day sale probability from {p0} to {p1}. Expected improvement: {net}.
explain.keepSeason: This unit has been in {store} for {age} days. High season is coming: demand over the next 90 days is {season} above the yearly average, with Buen Fin and December. Moving it to {best} would cost {cost} and change the expected result by {gain}. Waiting is the better choice.
explain.keepPlain: This unit has been in {store} for {age} days. Sale probability in 60 days: {p60}. No alternative improves the expected result by more than {threshold}. Keeping it is the better choice.
explain.keepBlocked: This unit has been in {store} for {age} days. A better option exists ({option}, {gain}), but it does not fit this week's plan because of capacity or higher-value units.
explain.leastLoss: This unit has been in {from} for {age} days and every option loses money over 90 days. Transferring it to {to} loses the least: {ev} versus {keepEv} if it stays. It sells {ratio} times faster there.

how.title: How it works
how.subtitle: From data to decision in five steps
how.step1Desc: Sales, inventory and costs from every dealership.
how.step2Desc: How many units of each model each dealership sells per month.
how.step3Desc: How soon each unit sells at every eligible dealership.
how.step4Desc: Floorplan, margin, transfer and discount, in pesos.
how.step5Desc: The highest-value actions that fit real operations.
how.tech1: 24 months of sales by dealership, model, trim and color. Inventory by VIN with arrival date, cost and list price. Floorplan rate, cost per km and receiving capacity.
how.tech2: Gamma-Poisson hierarchical model by dealership and model. Prior: group rate × traffic × brand affinity, with strength set by empirical Bayes (method of moments). Recency half-life of 6 months, monthly seasonality by segment and a launch trend for new brands.
how.tech3: Configuration rate = model rate × P(trim | dealership) × P(color | dealership), Dirichlet-smoothed toward the group, divided by the place in line among identical units (FIFO). Seasonal hazard: P(T ≤ t) = 1 − exp(−∫λ(s)ds).
how.tech4: 90-day expected value = P(sale) × (margin − discount) − expected floorplan − transfer − expected penalty for crossing 180 days. Discount response: exp(elasticity × discount).
how.tech5: Greedy by marginal improvement with a priority queue and lazy re-scoring: each accepted transfer updates the line at origin and destination. Respects weekly capacity, receiving space, minimum display, same franchise and maximum discount. Ends with a local improvement pass.
how.backtestSub: Fit on months 1 to 21. Forecast of months 22 to 24 by dealership and model.
how.naiveNote: Baseline: average of the last 3 months.
how.poolingSubOne: {model} in {store} had {months} month of sales at the cutoff. The pooled estimate borrows strength from the rest of the group.
how.poolingSubMany: {model} in {store} had {months} months of sales at the cutoff. The pooled estimate borrows strength from the rest of the group.
